item.title: Kadavu women rise above adversity
item.description: ROUND five of the Subrails Marama Championship produced several high-scoring encounters, with Nadi and Macuata sharing the spoils in a 22-all draw. Nadroga secured a 33-24 victory over Nasinu, Tailevu also recorded a 41-15 victory over Naitasiri, while Suva dominated Rewa 47-5. Namosi completed the round with a 51-34 win over Ba.
item.content:encoded:
ROUND five of the Subrails Marama Championship produced several high-scoring encounters, with Nadi and Macuata sharing the spoils in a 22-all draw.

Nadroga secured a 33-24 victory over Nasinu, Tailevu also recorded a 41-15 victory over Naitasiri, while Suva dominated Rewa 47-5. Namosi completed the round with a 51-34 win over Ba.

Kadavu women turned adversity into determination as they powered to a convincing 41-15 victory over Lautoka in Round Five of the Subrails Marama Championship at Churchill Park.

Kadavu coach Etuate Nauro said the team’s preparation was far from ideal, with persistent rain, limited access to suitable training grounds and the challenge of travelling from Kadavu to Lautoka.

Despite those setbacks, Nauro said the players remained committed and delivered a strong performance.

“We came through after a lot of challenges and struggles back in Kadavu. The weather was rainy, we couldn’t find a good ground to train on, also considering the travelling time to Lautoka.”

“We thank the girls for all the effort they have shown us,” Nauro said.

Kadavu made a strong start and dominated the opening half with powerful attacking and defensive play. Meredani Qoro scored two tries, while Sereima Rauqe and Salanieta Navatasi scored one try each. Matelita Nunia converted two tries as Kadavu went into halftime with a commanding 24-0 lead.

Kadavu continued to control possession and attack in the second half, scoring three more tries through Vatiseva Cavuru, Matelita Nunia and Ulumila Likubai. Livia Senibulileka converted one try.

Lautoka regrouped after halftime and managed to score three tries through Lotaini Loalala, Ruth Tinai and Camari Tora. However, Kadavu maintained their composure to secure an impressive 41-15 victory.

item.title: Yat Sen, St Joseph’s claim U19 titles
item.description: THE Yat Sen Secondary School’s boys team and St Joseph’s Secondary School’s girls team were crowned the under-19 basketball champions after winning their respective finals at the Vodafone Fiji Secondary School Basketball Championship at Vodafone Arena last Saturday. Yat Sen defeated Swami Vivekananda College (SVC) 25-17 in the U19 boys’ final, ending SVC’s impressive run in the competition.
item.content:encoded:
THE Yat Sen Secondary School’s boys team and St Joseph’s Secondary School’s girls team were crowned the under-19 basketball champions after winning their respective finals at the Vodafone Fiji Secondary School Basketball Championship at Vodafone Arena last Saturday.

Yat Sen defeated Swami Vivekananda College (SVC) 25-17 in the U19 boys’ final, ending SVC’s impressive run in the competition.

SVC coach Samisoni Vugakoto, who also helps coach the school’s U15 team, said the Nadi-based side was proud of the opportunity to compete against the established Suva schools.

“It was a tough game for us. We came down knowing that we were an underdog. In Nadi we don’t have facilities like they have here in Suva,” Vugakoto said.

He said the tournament provided valuable exposure for the players.

“We are so grateful Basketball Fiji is organising these events to give an opportunity for our children from Nadi to expose themselves in this competition and the venues like this.”

Vugakoto said the team entered the tournament as an unknown side but grew in confidence with every match.

“We entered the tournament as an underdog, an unknown. Then we just tried to maintain that we are here to become top dog,” he said.

In the U19 girls final, St Joseph’s Secondary School pulled off an upset narrowly edging the defending champions Adi Cakobau School 19-13 at Vodafone Arena in Suva.

St Joseph produced a determined performance to deny ACS another championship and claim the U19 girls’ title.

item.title: United mission | Different paths leading to one team, one dream
item.description: THE Junior Bula Boys may have come through different football pathways, but coach Marika Rodu says they must now put those differences aside and work as one team. The 23-member squad are in Samoa for the OFC U19 Men’s Championship.
item.content:encoded:
THE Junior Bula Boys may have come through different football pathways, but coach Marika Rodu says they must now put those differences aside and work as one team.

The 23-member squad are in Samoa for the OFC U19 Men’s Championship.

The team consists of players from Fiji’s professional setup; the Extra Premier League, the Senior Division and overseas leagues.

Nine players are based overseas, while four are members of Bula FC.

One player was selected from the Senior Division, while nine have played in Fiji’s Extra Premier League.

The squad also features players with previous national age-group experience, including two members of the 2024 U19 team and seven players from the U17 setup.

Rodu said the mixture had created a squad with different experiences but one common objective.

“We come from different football experiences. There are four from Bula FC, one from the Senior Division, nine from overseas and four will make their first trip,” Rodu said.

For Rodu, the key to bringing the group together is humility.

“Humbleness is key for us to make sure that we remind ourselves that we are one team.”

The team has spent six weeks preparing for the tournament, with Rodu believing the players are ready for the challenge.

“Across the board, we have a mixture of boys with experience, and I think we have the confidence to deliver the goods when we start playing on the second.”

item.title: Kadavu stun Lautoka in Skipper Cup thriller
item.description: KADAVU produced a courageous performance to upset Lautoka 13-12 in a thrilling Skipper Cup Round Five match at Churchill Park on Saturday night. Kadavu showed determination, courage and strength from the opening whistle, putting up a fierce attacking and defensive effort to frustrate the home side.
item.content:encoded:
KADAVU produced a courageous performance to upset Lautoka 13-12 in a thrilling Skipper Cup Round Five match at Churchill Park on Saturday night.

Kadavu showed determination, courage and strength from the opening whistle, putting up a fierce attacking and defensive effort to frustrate the home side.

Nacanieli Ratu scored Kadavu’s only try, while fullback Apisai Sokini converted and added a crucial penalty. Lautoka responded with a try through Nemani Camainakelo, but Kadavu held firm to take a 10-5 lead into halftime.

The second half saw pressure mount on both sides as Lautoka fought desperately to turn the match around.

Lautoka scored its second try through Eroni Leone, with Netava Bosenawai adding the conversion to put the home side in front.

However, Kadavu refused to surrender, with Sokini keeping his composure to slot a crucial penalty that ultimately secured the 13-12 victory.

Kadavu vice-captain Vaione Tegu said the team drew strength from their faith when Lautoka mounted its comeback.

“In that second half when Lautoka was fighting back, we reminded ourselves with this Bible verse, John 3:6. I kept telling the boys to be strong and keep pushing forward,” Tegu said.

“It was a good game and we thank Lautoka for a good game.”

item.title: MSG push | Battle Of Giants to sharpen preparations
item.description: THE 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants (BOG) tournament will provide Fiji’s players with a valuable platform to prepare for the Melanesian Spearhead Group (MSG) Cup, according to Fiji Football Association president Rajesh Patel. The BOG kicks off this Friday, September 4, with all pool matches scheduled to be played until Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
THE 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants (BOG) tournament will provide Fiji’s players with a valuable platform to prepare for the Melanesian Spearhead Group (MSG) Cup, according to Fiji Football Association president Rajesh Patel.

The BOG kicks off this Friday, September 4, with all pool matches scheduled to be played until Sunday.

The semi-finals and final will be held the following weekend on September 12 and 13 at Ba’s 4R Stadium, with Patel expecting another highly competitive contest between the participating teams.

Patel said the intensity of the BOG would benefit both the players and the national team’s preparations for the MSG tournament, which will be hosted in Fiji after the domestic competition on September 17 to October 3.

“It’s very competitive. Until the last day, people don’t know who’s going to win. So you cannot take any team lightly,” Patel said.

He said the competitiveness of the tournament meant players would need to remain focused throughout, while the format would also allow them enough time to recover between matches.

“It gives rest time to the players too. We know that this will help for the MSG preparation, which is coming up after the BOG,” Patel said.

Patel believes the BOG will give national coach Stephen Auvray an important opportunity to assess players in a competitive environment before finalising his plans for the MSG tournament.

He said the tournament could also help Auvray identify players for the Bula FC side, adding to the importance of the competition for Fiji’s football development.

This Friday fixtures will see Suva and Navua kicking off the tournament at 1pm, followed by Labasa taking on Nasinu FC at 3pm.

Rewa plays Lautoka at 5pm followed by the opening ceremony at 7pm.

Hosts Ba will take on Nadi at 7.30pm to conclude day one.

item.title: 14 provinces, one dream
item.description: Veiyasana Knight gives overlooked young league players a chance to chase their dreams For Veiyasana Knight under-17 coach Apisalome Nabose, missing out on selection for an established rugby league club should not mean the end of a young player’s dream.
item.content:encoded:
Veiyasana Knight gives overlooked young league players a chance to chase their dreams

For Veiyasana Knight under-17 coach Apisalome Nabose, missing out on selection for an established rugby league club should not mean the end of a young player’s dream.

The newly formed club is providing that second chance, defeating Topline Warriors 12-4 in round nine of the Eastern State Rugby League club competition.

Nabose and his father, who were among the founders of Davuilevu Knights, established the club to give aspiring players who could not make clubs such as Davuilevu Knights, Makoi Bulldogs and Nadera Panthers an opportunity to continue playing.

Nabose said the club’s name reflected its purpose.

“Veiyasana means for every province,” he said.

The aim is to cater for players from all 14 provinces of Fiji.

The response has been overwhelming, with players travelling from as far as Navutulevu in Serua, Nabukavesi in Namosi, Noco in Rewa, Lami and the interior of Tailevu for training and matches.

Without a proper training ground, the club trains every Tuesday and Thursday at Saint Joseph the Worker Primary School in Nakasi, with Nabose thanking the school for allowing the team to use its grounds.

Despite the long journeys, players continue to attend consistently and give their all at training.

“They come and train the house down,” Nabose said.

Their commitment has made selecting the 17-member match-day squad difficult.

With no financial sponsor this season, Nabose and his father also pay the players’ return fares for training and match days.

For Nabose, the sacrifice is worthwhile because rugby league can provide another pathway for young people seeking a future.

“Most of my players are not gifted inside the classrooms, so this opportunity is something big for them,” he said.

He hopes the players can eventually secure opportunities overseas and build careers through rugby league.

Nabose is now calling on companies and organisations to support the club next season as it seeks to give more young players an opportunity to make a name for themselves.

item.title: Fijiana sharpen basics
item.description: THE Vodafone Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker says the side is using its preparation period to sharpen the basics as it builds towards a one-off Test against Japan on September 4. The Fijiana XV squad trained in Nadi yesterday as preparations continued for the important international fixture before the team heads to Hong Kong for the WXV Global Series Challenger from September 13 to 26.
item.content:encoded:
THE Vodafone Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker says the side is using its preparation period to sharpen the basics as it builds towards a one-off Test against Japan on September 4.

The Fijiana XV squad trained in Nadi yesterday as preparations continued for the important international fixture before the team heads to Hong Kong for the WXV Global Series Challenger from September 13 to 26.

Walker said the team had spent the week learning, consolidating its work and addressing areas that needed improvement following its recent Test against South Africa.

“It’s been good. This week’s been full of learning and in the last couple of days we’ve tried to consolidate some of that learning,” Walker said.

He said the coaching staff had identified several areas they wanted to improve and had worked hard to bring those changes into the team’s current campaign.

Walker believes the squad possesses enough natural talent to create opportunities but stressed that the players must first execute the fundamentals.

“The ability that we’ll carry to play in space, to play with flair, it’s not something that I need to worry about. My focus is making sure that we do the basics really well,” he said.

That means making tackles consistently, retaining possession and showing patience when building attacking phases.

Walker said if the players could control those aspects of their game, opportunities to score would come naturally.

The Fijiana XV coach is also expecting a demanding challenge from Japan, describing them as a fast, structured and disciplined side.

He said Fiji would need to be sharp and clinical in possession while ensuring support players arrive quickly at breakdowns. He added Japan would be relentless throughout the 80 minutes. Walker believes controlling possession and gradually wearing Japan down will be crucial as Fijiana XV continues its preparations for the Test.

item.title: Malolo hold off Ba fight back in Lautoka
item.description: MALOLO Rugby held their nerve to secure a hard-fought 25-22 victory over Vinod Patel Ba Rugby Union at Churchill Park Ground Three yesterday. Malolo went into halftime with a commanding 15-0 lead after dominating the opening 40 minutes with strong attacking play and a solid defensive effort.
item.content:encoded:
MALOLO Rugby held their nerve to secure a hard-fought 25-22 victory over Vinod Patel Ba Rugby Union at Churchill Park Ground Three yesterday.

Malolo went into halftime with a commanding 15-0 lead after dominating the opening 40 minutes with strong attacking play and a solid defensive effort.

However, Ba returned from the break with renewed determination and mounted a strong fightback, putting Malolo under pressure in the second half.

The home side’s resurgence made for a tense finish, but Malolo managed to withstand the pressure and hold on for the three-point victory.

Malolo captain Imanueli Bari praised his teammates for their effort and credited Ba for providing a tough challenge.

“I thank the Ba team for giving us a good challenge and giving us a good game.

“It was a tough second half, and I thank the Malolo boys for a great effort. Now we will go back and regroup, ” Bari said.

Malolo will now turn their attention to their next assignment as they look to build on the hard-earned victory.
